findings.title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
findings.body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Bookings with a missing/disconnected destination calendar therefore fail during event creation.

findings.title: Select the destination belonging to the current credential
findings.body: EventManager now calls this service separately for each collective host but passes the entire destinationCalendar array each time. This service always uses the first host's calendar ID, including when authenticated as another host. With distinct Office 365 accounts, secondary-host event creation targets an inaccessible calendar and fails. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element problem; these services must select by the credential being used or receive an event containing only its destination.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
findings.body: The reference builder now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credentialId supplied by createMeeting. Cancellation only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other dedicated video meetings will no longer be deleted when their bookings are cancelled.

findings.title: Restore a usable calendar fallback for references without an external ID
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or missing, the new fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same null/missing value, which cannot match a normal destination. Google updateEvent consequently receives no calendarId and fails for older references lacking an externalCalendarId, even when the event has a valid destination. The analogous deleteEvent change falls back to primary rather than the configured destination, leaving events on non-primary calendars undeleted.

findings.title: Initialize the destination array before adding collective hosts
findings.body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently drops all teamDestinationCalendars, even if the other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no calendar events; the array should still contain their destinations when the organizer has none.

findings.title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's own credential
findings.body: For an all-remaining recurring cancellation, the code ignores the credential resolved for the current reference and instead loops only over the booking owner's credentials, deleting only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. The outer loop repeats this operation for every host rather than deleting each host's reference. Secondary collective hosts' recurring events therefore remain on their calendars even though all bookings are marked cancelled.

findings.title: Do not reverse the billing-dependent organization slug condition
findings.body: This unrelated change reverses the condition for persisting the organization slug: installations with team billing disabled now create organizations without a slug, while billing-enabled installations immediately persist the requested slug. Previously the former received the slug and the latter stored only requestedSlug in metadata. This breaks organization URL provisioning on non-billing installations and bypasses the deferred slug assignment behavior on billing-enabled installations.
